page: Vultr vcg-a40-2c-10g-4vram is a fractional GPU instance within the Cloud GPU family. It features an Intel x86_64 processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading, operating at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 10.0 GB of system memory, 180 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU providing 4 GB of dedicated VRAM.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance split. The instance exhibits strong capabilities in LLM prompt processing, achieving 3480.67 tokens/sec for a small 135M model and 202.17 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. However, general compute and memory performance are limited. Stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25% tier, while Passmark database operations register in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds categorized as weak.

This instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads by utilizing a fractional GPU slice rather than a full dedicated card. This resource density makes it highly suitable for lightweight machine learning inference, small-scale model testing, and development tasks. It is less suited for heavy database operations, high-throughput web serving, or memory-intensive multi-core processing due to its lower CPU and memory performance profiles.
